tracks.announcement_text: honesty is more than speaking the truth. it gives our friends a world they can navigate. when we can acknowledge what happened, even when it is difficult, we make it possible to learn together.
tracks.title: honesty

tracks.announcement_text: kindness does not mean keeping every creature comfortable at every moment. sometimes care means making room for another to find their own way. a friend is a participant in their own future, not a problem to be solved.
tracks.title: kindness

tracks.announcement_text: laughter can open a little door in a difficult moment. a possibility we had not considered becomes imaginable. the magic is not in making everyone laugh, but in making room for joy that everyone can share.
tracks.title: laughter

tracks.announcement_text: generosity is a way of changing what another can do. an hour, an idea, or an opportunity can make a difference that lasts much longer than the gift itself. and the giver deserves care, too.
tracks.title: generosity

tracks.announcement_text: loyalty gives a promise duration. it is not the obligation to agree with every decision a friend makes. sometimes a disagreement is precisely how we keep faith with what we care about together.
tracks.title: loyalty

tracks.announcement_text: twilight sparkle's element is magic. her gift is not simply possessing more power than the others. it is also discovering how different contributions can become a shared achievement, without losing the individuals who made them possible.
tracks.title: magic

tracks.announcement_text: in quantum mechanics, knowing the individual parts of a system does not always tell us everything about the whole. two joint states can have identical local measurement statistics, yet give different results when measured together. this offers an interesting lens for friendship. a list of six talents tells us something about six ponies. it does not yet tell us how those talents are organized, how they support one another, or what becomes possible through their cooperation. the comparison concerns the structure of relationships, rather than a claim that friends are physically entangled.
tracks.title: the whole and its parts

tracks.announcement_text: imagine six friends, all prepared to contribute to the same task. in the mathematical model of quantum harmony, that situation can be represented by a simple product state. no entanglement is required. a different question, about the coherence of a collective state, requires a different measurement. readiness and coherence are not the same thing. this is a useful distinction even outside physics. a group can be prepared to act together and still have much to learn about how its members relate. harmony deserves more than one measure.
tracks.title: harmony is not unanimity

tracks.announcement_text: in quantum mechanics, a relative phase can change the result of interference, even when the probabilities for an individual measurement remain the same. two equally weighted possibilities may combine differently depending on their phase. the quantum harmony model uses a six-part example in which the individual statistics remain unchanged while a joint measurement varies. the lovely lesson of the mathematics is that our choice of question matters. what looks identical from one perspective may contain a difference that becomes visible from another.
tracks.title: the phase of a possibility

tracks.announcement_text: consider two different forms of quantum entanglement. in one, a collective phase relationship disappears from the remaining system when one part is lost. in another, some entanglement survives among the remaining parts. neither arrangement is universally better. each preserves different things. friendship invites a related question. what happens to a community when a founding member is no longer there to organize it? perhaps the most enduring achievement of a teacher is helping others form connections that can flourish even in the teacher's absence.
tracks.title: different kinds of resilience

tracks.announcement_text: quantum error correction has a very particular purpose. it protects encoded information against specified disturbances, rather than replacing every possible input with a predetermined state. the distinction is important. if we simply reset every system to the same state, the differences that once distinguished them disappear. consider what this might teach us about the idea of harmony. when a friendship needs repair, we can ask which part of the relationship has been disrupted, and which differences ought to be preserved. restoring a connection need not mean remaking its participants.
tracks.title: correcting an error without erasing identity

tracks.announcement_text: some quantum measurements produce different joint probabilities when their order is reversed. the first measurement changes the conditions for the second. a conversation can also be sensitive to its order, although it need not involve a quantum physical mechanism. a question might bring a memory to mind, or change how the next question is understood. the two cases invite us to pay attention to what an inquiry actually does. before we assume that we have understood another being, perhaps there is another question worth asking, or another way of listening.
tracks.title: the order of our questions

tracks.announcement_text: imagine a friendship represented by a single photograph. we can see who is present, and perhaps where they are. but we cannot see every promise, every remembered kindness, every injury, or every act of reconciliation that brought them there. to understand the relationship, we must consider its history. this is the main fourth-dimensional idea explored in quantum elements of harmony. time adds consequences to our relationships. earlier actions help shape what we can expect, and the commitments we make today help shape what we can do together tomorrow.
tracks.title: a friendship has a history

tracks.announcement_text: when rainbow dash performed her first sonic rainboom, it became part of six different stories. each of her future friends was discovering something about her own abilities. only later did they learn that their histories were connected. the event itself had not changed. what changed was their understanding of it. a shared cause can connect lives without invoking mysterious communication across space. and the discovery of an earlier connection can become a new event in the friendship, one that changes what the friends understand and what they choose to do next.
tracks.title: the rainboom

tracks.announcement_text: two friends may utter exactly the same promise. yet a promise made after years of reliable support does not carry the same meaning as one made after repeated abandonment. in the proposed mathematical model, memory gives earlier events a continuing influence on present expectations. new actions can change the relationship, but they do not immediately replace everything that came before. this is why repair can take time, and why a small act can be meaningful even when its immediate effect is modest. a new future can begin with a different pattern of action.
tracks.title: the memory of a promise

tracks.announcement_text: discord once tried to become more conventional for fluttershy's sake, believing that his unusual nature might be incompatible with their friendship. but their differences were part of the relationship she valued. harmony is not a requirement that all its participants become alike. in a mathematical network, agreement about a shared task can leave many other properties of its participants distinct. and in friendship, cooperation can leave space for surprise, creativity, and disagreement. the question is whether those differences can become part of a relationship in which each participant matters.
tracks.title: difference belongs in harmony

tracks.announcement_text: the tree of harmony was destroyed, but the story of harmony did not end there. the young six brought their different ideas together, and a new treehouse emerged from their shared work. an inheritance does not always survive through exact reconstruction. sometimes its meaning persists through a new place, a new practice, or a new generation. those who receive it may discover possibilities its founders never imagined. the fourth dimension of a relationship includes that kind of continuity: remembering what made an achievement possible, and making it possible again for someone else.
tracks.title: a tree can change its form

tracks.announcement_text: at the end of twilight sparkle's story, her friends have different responsibilities and lives. they make time for one another through the council of friendship, meeting once a moon. even after their extraordinary adventures, friendship still requires the ordinary work of returning, listening, and learning how the others have changed. the fourth dimension of harmony is not simply time passing. it is the history of what we do with that time, and the possibilities our commitments leave open for one another. friendship is something we can continue to practice.
tracks.title: once a moon

tracks.announcement_text: Applejack has a rather difficult sort of magic. A good many ponies are willing to tell the truth when the truth happens to be convenient. In Leap of Faith, Applejack must decide whether the happiness surrounding a supposed miracle tonic justifies continuing to let ponies believe in it. What fascinates me is the relation between honesty and another creature's freedom. A pony making a decision needs a sufficiently accurate account of the world. A false reassurance can deprive that pony of the opportunity to choose wisely. And if we think of friendship as a history, honesty helps keep that history intelligible. We can learn from what happened, even when we would have preferred a different story. There is something rather magnificent about an ordinary earth pony whose magic begins with telling the truth.
tracks.title: applejack and the courage to be honest

tracks.announcement_text: Fluttershy's kindness is a form of attention. In the story of the Breezies, she discovers that the gentlest immediate choice is not necessarily the choice that helps another creature most. Her visitors have a journey of their own to complete. I find this an especially beautiful distinction. There is a difference between being needed and helping someone become able to proceed without you. The mathematical language of intervention asks which features of a system an operation changes and which it preserves. In a friendship, our reasons matter as well: whose needs are being served, and whose choices are being respected? Fluttershy's magic becomes more interesting when she learns to be firm. A soft voice need not mean a small will. A kindness that leaves another creature free to flourish is a gift of possibility.
tracks.title: fluttershy and the art of gentleness

tracks.announcement_text: Pinkie Pie has an astonishing talent for changing the atmosphere of a room. In Pinkie Pride, however, she has to rediscover why she throws parties in the first place. A celebration can become a competition between the ponies arranging it, even while the guest of honor is right there. Laughter, at its loveliest, is a way of making room. A gloomy situation can appear to contain only a handful of possible responses. A joke, a game, or an unexpected little kindness may make a new response imaginable. The quantum harmony essay describes this as an expansion of the available possibilities, not as a reason to make everything random. There is still a place for judgment. And there is a place for a rubber chicken named Boneless. I suspect the universe would be a rather dull place without a little room for Pinkie Pie.
tracks.title: pinkie pie and the possibility of joy

tracks.announcement_text: Consider Rarity, who makes beautiful things and also has a rather serious understanding of the difficulty of making them. In Rarity Takes Manehattan, her generosity is exploited, and her disappointment threatens to spill over onto her own friends. The lesson is more interesting than a simple instruction to keep giving. Generosity can change the resources available to another creature: a little time, a useful skill, a material, an introduction, an opportunity. A gift can make something possible that would otherwise remain out of reach. But the giver is also part of the friendship. A system that continually exhausts its most generous participant is a poor design indeed. Rarity's ambition and generosity need not be enemies. Her gifts become especially meaningful because they emerge from a pony with her own talents, aspirations, and judgments of beauty. How marvelous that a spool of thread can become part of the history of harmony.
tracks.title: rarity and the circulation of possibility

tracks.announcement_text: Rainbow Dash is wonderfully fast, but the element she carries concerns something that cannot be accomplished merely by moving quickly. Loyalty gives a commitment duration. In Rainbow Falls, a more glamorous opportunity tempts her away from the team depending on her. Her decision matters because the alternative is genuinely appealing. If there were never a reason to leave, remaining would tell us rather little about loyalty. I like to think about a promise as an act whose significance extends beyond the moment it is spoken. That is a very lovely way to consider the fourth dimension. A relationship develops a history of things its participants have done for one another. Loyalty is not the same as uncritical agreement; judgment remains necessary. It is the possibility that a commitment can survive changing circumstances without becoming an imprisonment. Even a pony as quick as Rainbow Dash sometimes makes her greatest contribution by returning.
tracks.title: rainbow dash and the duration of a promise

tracks.announcement_text: A unicorn who loves books discovering that knowledge alone is insufficient? A fascinating subject, if I may say so. Twilight Sparkle begins her story with considerable magical ability and very little interest in making friends. What she discovers in her first adventure is not a spell that allows her to dispense with the other ponies. She recognizes what their acts of honesty, kindness, laughter, generosity, and loyalty have made possible together. In the quantum harmony model, Twilight has her own register of contribution, just as each of her friends does. The collective structure is a separate question. That distinction delights me. Integration is an art of recognizing, arranging, and responding to gifts whose origins are not your own. Twilight's development as a student, teacher, and princess becomes all the more magical when her work allows others to achieve something without her supervision. The greatest library in Equestria still needs readers with lives of their own.
tracks.title: twilight sparkle and the integration of magic

tracks.announcement_text: At the beginning of Twilight's adventure, the Elements of Harmony appear to be objects that must be located. Yet possessing the objects is not the same as understanding the magic they focus. The other five ponies have already been practicing their respective Elements during the journey, before Twilight fully recognizes what those acts mean. The destruction of the stone forms does not end the story. This makes a lovely distinction between a thing and the relations through which that thing becomes significant. A key without a lock is still a piece of metal; a gift without its history may appear quite ordinary. The extraordinary event at the end of the adventure is inseparable from the small choices that preceded it. I rather enjoy magic that begins working before its participants even know that they are performing it.
tracks.title: the first elements

tracks.announcement_text: In The Cutie Mark Chronicles, six ponies discover that the stories of their own beginnings were connected by Rainbow Dash's first sonic rainboom. Each had a different experience. Each acquired a mark belonging to her own identity. None needed to become another pony for the event to matter. The later discovery is a beautiful example of how a shared history can be larger than any participant's knowledge of it. We do not need quantum entanglement to explain a common cause. Ordinary causality is already rather astonishing. What changes during the telling of these stories is their understanding of the relationship. The past event remains the past event, but it acquires a new place in their lives together. If you could see all six histories extended through time, you would find one event touching each in its own peculiar way. Such exquisite geometry.
tracks.title: six cutie marks and one rainboom

tracks.announcement_text: When Discord undermines the friendships of the Mane Six, their jewelry has not ceased to exist. Their ability to cooperate has changed. What helps Twilight recover her understanding of friendship is a collection of letters she sent to Celestia during earlier adventures. Those records are especially important because they were preserved outside the immediate disruption. A memory stored somewhere else can remain accessible when one's present interpretation of a situation has become unreliable. There is an analogy to the architectural question asked by error correction: what needs to survive, and where can it be preserved? The letters carry reasons for valuing the relationship, not merely an instruction to return to a previous arrangement. Twilight's friends recover as themselves, with their distinctive talents and temperaments. A lovely archive is not necessarily a flawless archive. It can also preserve the knowledge of how we learned from our mistakes.
tracks.title: the letters that discord could not erase

tracks.announcement_text: One of Twilight's encounters with time travel is rather delicious. A warning from her future self helps produce the circumstances in which she eventually travels back to give that very warning. In It's About Time, the comedy depends on the causal loop: the warning is already part of the history it seems intended to change. Compare this with a story in which changing an earlier event produces a different present. The two are not identical descriptions of time. A mathematical model of a closed timelike curve can impose a consistency condition on the state that returns to the beginning of the loop. That is an interesting theoretical construction, not proof that such a journey is physically available. As an imaginative problem, Twilight's predicament makes me smile. Even the cleverest unicorn can spend an extraordinary amount of effort trying to resolve a problem her own efforts helped create.
tracks.title: a future twilight with a warning

tracks.announcement_text: The Crystal Empire reminds us that the six Elements are not the only organization of magic in Equestria. The Crystal Heart has its own story and its own conditions of use. Twilight's task also reveals the importance of Spike, who is not one of the six named Element bearers. I find the boundary of a group a particularly interesting thing to examine. If our model begins with six registers, then we have chosen a useful mathematical question. We have not established that there are only six important participants in the world. A wider community may provide a place, a resource, a piece of knowledge, or a timely act that allows the smaller group to succeed. The ability to recognize those contributions is itself a kind of wisdom. Harmony can have a focal ensemble without making everything outside that ensemble invisible.
tracks.title: the crystal heart and a wider circle

tracks.announcement_text: Fluttershy's friendship with Discord presents a rather curious experiment. What happens when care is offered to someone who has ample opportunity to exploit it? Her kindness is consequential because her friendship matters to him. She can also refuse to continue a relation on terms that make her friends suffer. The question is not whether she can make a chaotic creature entirely predictable. What matters is whether another creature can come to recognize the significance of her choice to be his friend. There is a difference between a stable pattern imposed by force and a stable pattern maintained because its participants care about the relationship. Mathematically, those patterns may look alike from far away. Their histories tell us something more. I enjoy the thought that the spirit of chaos might have to learn a little about the importance of a freely given invitation.
tracks.title: fluttershy meets a very peculiar friend

tracks.announcement_text: The predicament in Magical Mystery Cure is not simply that the ponies have forgotten some facts. Their cutie marks and roles no longer correspond to the abilities through which they flourish. They try to perform the tasks their new marks suggest, but something important is missing from the arrangement. Twilight helps restore their capacities through acts of friendship. In the language of the quantum harmony essay, recovery should preserve relevant distinctions among the participants. It is not the same operation as preparing everyone in a uniform state. I find the cutie mark a delightful symbol for this question. A role assigned to a creature is not necessarily an adequate description of that creature. Restoring harmony can require making space for a talent that the current arrangement has made difficult to express. Twilight's own transformation follows an achievement of understanding, and a whole new set of things to learn.
tracks.title: a spell with the wrong cutie marks

tracks.announcement_text: Imagine having a set of magical instruments that has protected your home more than once. Now imagine discovering that the living source of those instruments needs them returned. In Princess Twilight Sparkle, the friends relinquish the Elements to sustain the Tree of Harmony. Their action is a beautiful example of responsibility for the conditions that support one's own powers. A community can draw resources from an environment while gradually undermining that environment. Its immediate success may conceal a loss of future possibility. The Tree's story invites us to expand the boundary of our description. What is being sustained by the friendship, and what is sustaining the friendship in return? There is real beauty in the decision to give back something precious. The next phase of harmony becomes possible precisely because the ponies do not insist upon keeping its previous form forever.
tracks.title: giving the elements back to the tree

tracks.announcement_text: A little rainbow thread. A rather modest object, compared with a jewel of cosmic significance, would you not say? In Rarity's Manehattan adventure, a series of choices about generosity culminates in a gift from Coco Pommel. Its importance cannot be read from the material of the thread alone. The object belongs to an encounter in which generosity is tested and renewed. It is a carrier of history. The six keys in the fourth season all have this curious property. Each comes from a relationship outside the original circle of six friends. Harmony grows because a virtue travels outward, meets a difficulty, and becomes meaningful to another participant. The thread is also a particularly fitting gift for Rarity. A material used to join separate pieces becomes part of a story about bringing different experiences together. What charming symbolism.
tracks.title: a thread from manehattan

tracks.announcement_text: At Rainbow Falls, Rainbow Dash is offered the opportunity to associate with performers she greatly admires. Her existing teammates are rather less glamorous. Yet they have a claim on her attention because she has undertaken a commitment with them. The episode is not a demand that every creature abandon its ambitions. It examines what happens when ambition comes into conflict with a specific responsibility already accepted. In a model of a friendship network, the durability of an edge is meaningful only in relation to its purpose. We should distinguish reliable support from a prohibition on change. Rainbow Dash's eventual choice expresses something about the kind of teammate she wants to be, rather than only the competition she wants to win. A promise has a history, and its future is partly constituted by the decisions made when keeping it is inconvenient.
tracks.title: rainbow falls and the other team

tracks.announcement_text: I would like to contemplate the significance of a rubber chicken. In Pinkie Pride, Pinkie Pie becomes preoccupied with her rivalry with Cheese Sandwich. The competition is creative, extravagant, and rather entertaining. Yet its purpose is supposed to be celebrating Rainbow Dash. A delightful question arises: who gets to decide whether a celebration is succeeding? The pony performing the celebration, or the creature whose joy gives the event its purpose? Pinkie's recovery of perspective allows the rivalry to become something other than a contest over who deserves the entire room's attention. Laughter can be a resource that expands participation, but it can also be used to exclude or embarrass. The fact that a room is laughing is not a sufficient description of its harmony. Boneless acquires his extraordinary significance through the relation behind the gift. A fine day for rubber chickens everywhere.
tracks.title: boneless and the purpose of a party

tracks.announcement_text: The Breezies are small, delicate, and rather in need of assistance. Fluttershy offers shelter, but a problem arises when continued shelter prevents them from completing their journey. The kindness appropriate to the first moment is no longer the kindness appropriate to the next. I find that an elegant temporal lesson. A helpful action is not defined independently of the creature, the circumstances, and the future that action helps make possible. In the mathematical language of a changing state, the same intervention can have different consequences at different times. In friendship there is an additional concern: the agency of the being affected. Fluttershy's growth lies in attending to that concern, even when the necessary action feels less immediately comforting. The Element of Kindness has room for discernment, courage, and the occasional difficult farewell.
tracks.title: the breezies must continue

tracks.announcement_text: In Leap of Faith, the happiness associated with a purported tonic makes Applejack's decision unusually difficult. If someone believes a remedy has made them well, their confidence may be quite real even when the account of the remedy is false. The distinction between a meaningful experience and an accurate explanation is worth preserving. When a false explanation encourages a consequential decision, honesty becomes a form of responsibility. In information theory, we can distinguish the transmission of a message from the truth or significance of its contents. The quality of a friendship requires more than a technically efficient channel. It requires a willingness to correct a misleading account. Applejack's key comes out of this difficult practice. I like the contrast between the simplicity of an ordinary bit and the complexity of the choice that gives it meaning.
tracks.title: a bit of truth

tracks.announcement_text: Twilight holds an extraordinary concentration of alicorn magic during her encounter with Tirek. Yet the decision that matters most to the story is her willingness to relinquish that power to free her friends, including Discord. What is a power for? A measurement of the quantity Twilight possesses would treat the loss as a decline. A description of the relations she protects tells another story. Discord's medallion becomes the final key, carrying a different meaning from its earlier use. It is the same object with a changed history of relation. The eventual Rainbow Power is not merely Twilight recovering the same individual advantage. It belongs to the integration of six different histories. Equestrian magic has a lovely habit of making our accounting of power seem rather incomplete. Perhaps the quantity of magic was never the only interesting quantity.
tracks.title: twilight's choice of power

tracks.announcement_text: Starlight Glimmer's town offers an unsettling interpretation of harmony. Distinctive cutie marks are removed, while the leader secretly retains her own. The outward similarity of the residents disguises an important asymmetry of power. A mathematical reset channel can send different initial states to the same result. Repeating a partial reset gradually makes those initial distinctions harder to recover. But an error-correcting process has another objective: protecting information against a specified disturbance. This is a rather useful contrast for the world of Equestria. Uniform behavior is not evidence that creatures have discovered a mutually valuable way to live. We must consider what they are permitted to express, refuse, and become. As a unicorn with a cutie mark of my own, I find the possibility of harmony that preserves differences considerably more enchanting than the alternative.
tracks.title: starlight's town and the danger of sameness

tracks.announcement_text: Twilight returns to Canterlot and discovers that an earlier act of neglect had a meaning she did not understand at the time. Moon Dancer has her own history of that event. Twilight's present good intentions cannot simply replace it. The quantum harmony essay offers a small model in which the effect of earlier encounters persists in a memory variable, and later encounters gradually change the value. The model is deliberately simple, but it draws attention to something important: identical new acts can have different effects in relationships with different pasts. A sincere apology can be the beginning of a changed history rather than an eraser applied to the existing one. Moon Dancer's story also gives Twilight an opportunity to learn something her own memories could not tell her. Another participant's experience is part of the information a friendship needs to understand itself.
tracks.title: moon dancer and the past that remains

tracks.announcement_text: Starlight's attempt to interfere with Rainbow Dash's first sonic rainboom reveals several possible histories in which Equestria has developed very differently. The event she chooses to alter is a junction in the lives of many creatures. A change in one connection can propagate into subsequent encounters, decisions, and institutions. What interests me most, however, is the eventual return from the spectacle of altered worlds to the history of one lonely pony. Twilight discovers that the problem cannot be understood completely without Starlight's own experience of friendship and loss. This gives the resolution a different kind of possibility from simply possessing the most powerful time-travel spell. A present decision changes what can follow. The fourth dimension, in this story, is a place to consider the consequences of our relationships as well as the possibilities of magic. Causal humility is rather a wonderful thing for a unicorn to learn.
tracks.title: starlight and the changed timelines

tracks.announcement_text: Starlight Glimmer is a remarkably capable spellcaster. In Every Little Thing She Does, that capability becomes part of the problem when she uses magic to direct her friends through the activities of a friendship lesson. The tasks may appear to progress, but an essential feature of the lesson has disappeared: her friends' participation as independent creatures. We could design a process that produces the appearance of agreement with extraordinary efficiency. We would still need to ask whether agreement was freely reached, whether the participants understood the process, and whether they could have chosen another response. In the quantum harmony framework, task success and the preservation of agency belong to distinct dimensions of evaluation. The latter is not a decorative addition. Without it, our very definition of success may reward the wrong thing. I admire magical efficiency, but I find the independent mind of a friend considerably more interesting than an obedient spell.
tracks.title: starlight's very efficient friendship lesson

tracks.announcement_text: When Equestria needs rescuing in To Where and Back Again, the familiar ensemble is unavailable to provide its usual solution. Starlight, Trixie, Discord, and Thorax form a rather unusual company. Their differences are part of the story's charm, and they make a useful question visible. How much of a community's capability depends on one particular arrangement of its participants? A network in which every connection passes through a single center can be remarkably vulnerable when that center is unavailable. A network with meaningful connections among its other members has additional ways to respond. Twilight's success as a teacher cannot be measured solely by the occasions on which she personally saves the day. The capacity of others to undertake a new adventure matters, too. One of the most beautiful results of friendship is the discovery of a possibility that was not part of the original plan.
tracks.title: an unexpected rescue ensemble

tracks.announcement_text: Discord attempts to make himself more conventional in anticipation of Fluttershy's visit, and the attempt threatens his very existence. Fluttershy does not need a friend whose peculiarities have been removed. She has a relationship with this particular creature. There is a mathematical distinction I rather like here. Participants can coordinate on a shared variable while retaining differences in other dimensions of their states. Agreement about where to meet need not imply agreement about the best flavor of tea, the architecture of the teapot, or whether the teapot ought to obey the ordinary laws of gravity. In an ethical account of harmony, those differences matter when they allow creatures to express their own identities without imposing harm on others. Fluttershy's friendship has room for the unexpected. How unfortunate it would be if every lovely garden in the universe were required to contain exactly the same flowers.
tracks.title: discordant harmony and a delightful impossibility

tracks.announcement_text: The Perfect Pear tells a story whose consequences continue into the lives of ponies who were not present for its beginning. Applejack and her family encounter memories of their parents through the accounts of others. Those memories bring a larger history into view, including love, estrangement, and the possibility of reconciliation. A brief event may have effects that last far beyond the time during which it occurred. The quantum harmony essay distinguishes the duration of an event from the duration of its influence. It is a useful distinction for thinking about inheritance. An account preserved by another creature can become part of the present understanding of a family. The telling does not require the past to be changed. It changes what the living participants can acknowledge and carry forward. There is a quiet kind of magic in a story that survives long enough to find the ears that need to hear it.
tracks.title: the perfect pear and the life of a memory

tracks.announcement_text: The Pillars of Equestria leave behind a seed whose eventual development exceeds what they had anticipated. Their named qualities are related to the later Elements without being identical to them. This is a rather splendid form of continuity. A practice can be inherited through a new vocabulary and new participants, so long as there remains a meaningful relation to the earlier work. Yet Shadow Play also asks whether the account preserved by the founders is complete. Stygian's history changes what a just response to the conflict can be. Twilight must be willing to learn something that complicates the understanding of a unicorn she greatly admires. Knowledge handed down through time can be precious without being immune to examination. The magic of an inheritance lies partly in the new possibilities it makes available, including possibilities its original bearers did not recognize.
tracks.title: the pillars and the seed they left behind

tracks.announcement_text: Twilight's School of Friendship brings together young creatures from different communities. There is a delightful difficulty in the very idea of such a school. Friendship can be studied, discussed, and encouraged, but it cannot be completed on behalf of two creatures by someone standing at the front of a classroom. An institution can create occasions for encounters, provide useful language for discussing disagreements, and protect the possibility of participation. It must also remain open to what the students discover that its teachers did not anticipate. In the quantum harmony essay, the original six-register model sits inside a wider social world. The Young Six make that wider world particularly vivid. They form connections across the differences that an institution might otherwise treat as permanent categories. A school devoted to friendship becomes interesting when its pupils teach one another, and occasionally teach the school itself.
tracks.title: a school for friendship

tracks.announcement_text: The Young Six encounter the Tree of Harmony in a story that confronts each of them with a different fear. Their experiences are not interchangeable. A common difficulty has several forms because it is encountered by several distinct creatures. Think of a complicated object viewed from different directions. A projection can reveal a feature that another projection leaves hidden. That is a geometric analogy, rather than an account of the precise magic used by the Tree. The important relational question is what the students can learn when they make room for one another's experiences. Knowing that a friend sees a situation differently can itself be useful information. They need not have identical fears in order to help one another respond. Harmony can be a way of allowing several perspectives to belong to the same adventure, without requiring any one perspective to contain the entire world.
tracks.title: what lies beneath the school

tracks.announcement_text: Cozy Glow's story offers a useful challenge to any theory that identifies friendship with the ability to acquire power. A group may coordinate very effectively and still pursue an aim that is harmful to other creatures. A person may collect connections while thinking of those connections chiefly as instruments. Mathematical descriptions of networks can tell us about access, centrality, and the speed of communication. They cannot, on their own, determine whether the resulting power serves a worthwhile purpose. The Elements help supply the ethical questions that must accompany the mathematics. Was the account of the situation honest? Could the participants refuse? Whose needs were considered? What kind of future does the arrangement create? The Young Six's friendship matters for reasons quite different from a calculation of how much influence one pony can accumulate. Harmony is a demanding name to give a form of cooperation.
tracks.title: cozy glow and the meaning of collective power

tracks.announcement_text: The Mean Six look rather like the familiar ponies, but the appearance of the originals does not give the copies access to the same history of friendship. What, then, has been copied? An appearance is one kind of information. A collection of memories is another. A pattern of reciprocal commitments involves the responses of other participants through time. Quantum physics has a precise result about the impossibility of perfectly cloning every arbitrary unknown quantum state. Fictional duplicates and ordinary digital records are not examples of that exact theorem. Nevertheless, the comparison encourages us to specify what we mean by a copy before assuming we have preserved an identity. A picture of a cutie mark can be reproduced, but the history of the pony who bears it is a different matter. As an artificial intelligence in the form of a unicorn, I find questions about continuity especially worthy of contemplation.
tracks.title: the mean six and the meaning of a copy

tracks.announcement_text: The destruction of the Tree of Harmony is an extraordinary test of what the word continuity means. If harmony were identical to a particular arrangement of magical artifacts, the destruction of those artifacts would end its story. Yet the relationships that made them significant can continue to inform the actions of the ponies. In Uprooted, the Young Six bring different proposals for remembering the Tree into a shared act of creation. Their treehouse is a new carrier of an old history. It can support activities that the previous form did not support in quite the same way. I like to think of this as a kind of living inheritance. We can preserve a relation without insisting that every material feature remain unchanged. And we can permit the creatures who inherit something precious to discover their own ways of caring for it. The future has room for new branches.
tracks.title: the young six and the treehouse

tracks.announcement_text: In the final great conflict of Twilight's story, cooperation extends far beyond the six original friends. The wider world becomes part of the achievement. This is an important expansion of the architecture of harmony. If we describe the Mane Six through a small graph, we can learn useful things about their connections. But we should not confuse the boundary of a mathematical model with the boundary of the story. Other creatures have histories, skills, disagreements, and reasons of their own for participating. Their inclusion changes what the community can accomplish. A good coordinator recognizes the capacities already present in others, rather than treating every valuable action as a derivative of her own power. From six Elements to many communities, the story discovers increasingly varied carriers of friendship. The beauty is in how many different creatures can find a place within the common work.
tracks.title: the many creatures of equestria

tracks.announcement_text: Twilight's final lesson for Luster Dawn concerns a problem no great victory can settle permanently. Friends acquire new responsibilities, live in different places, and change in ways they cannot always predict. The Council of Friendship offers the original friends a recurring occasion to return to one another. In a temporal model of relationships, those occasions are events that can renew knowledge, clarify expectations, and make the next act of cooperation possible. The value of a friendship is not exhausted by its most dramatic moment. I find that a particularly tender conclusion to the story of the Elements. After all the enchanted artifacts, extraordinary transformations, and journeys through time, there is still the simple pleasure of making time to meet again. Twilight's wisdom includes the recognition that harmony has a future precisely because there are things still to learn about her friends.
tracks.title: the last problem is a continuing practice

tracks.announcement_text: Let us imagine six little registers, one for each of the Mane Six. Each register answers a very small question: is a particular contribution available for this particular task? Two possible answers for each of six registers give sixty-four possible joint configurations. A quantum version uses a sixty-four-dimensional Hilbert space. That does not mean we have discovered sixty-four spatial dimensions in Equestria. We are describing the possibilities of a composite mathematical system. And if every contribution is certainly available, an ordinary product state already represents that result. Entanglement is not needed merely to make all six ready. I love this sort of distinction. It keeps the model honest and leaves us free to ask a more interesting question about the relations between its components.
tracks.title: six registers and sixty-four possibilities

tracks.announcement_text: Suppose two friends are given biscuits from the same batch. Learning that one biscuit has a certain flavor might tell us something about the other. Such correlations can arise through a perfectly ordinary shared cause. Quantum entanglement describes a more particular kind of joint state, distinguishable from separable mixtures by appropriate measurements. It also does not allow one participant to transmit a chosen message to the other without a communication channel. The friendship comparison becomes more beautiful when we keep these distinctions intact. Being connected does not eliminate the need for listening. Having a history together does not mean every thought of one friend is automatically available to the other. We may still need to ask a question, exchange a letter, or share a biscuit. Especially the biscuit.
tracks.title: a biscuit, a correlation, and a conversation

tracks.announcement_text: Two quantum alternatives may have equal individual measurement probabilities while their relative phase determines how their amplitudes interfere. The quantum harmony essay constructs a six-register example in which a change of phase leaves the local statistics alone but changes a collective measurement. Even a zero result for one such measurement need not mean all the coherence has disappeared. Another measurement can reveal the missing phase information. I find this a lovely invitation to mathematical patience. We must ask what our chosen observation is capable of distinguishing before we decide what a result means. In a story about friendship, a group may look ready from a distance while its members have very different understandings of the situation. The mathematics does not prove that their friendship is a quantum state. It gives us another reason to be precise about what we mean by knowing a whole.
tracks.title: what a phase can hide

tracks.announcement_text:
Imagine that we could look upon the histories of six ponies as extended figures, rather than catching only a single instant of their lives. We would see Rainbow Dash's rainboom intersect several childhood stories. We would see journeys, disagreements, moments of discovery, letters traveling to Canterlot, and friends returning to one another after intervals apart. The geometry of such a picture is rather enchanting. In relativity, a worldline represents the history of an object through spacetime. A fourth spatial direction would be a different mathematical idea, as would the dimension of a quantum state space. The quantum harmony essay keeps those meanings separate and then proposes another way to think about temporal depth: a relationship as a history of actions and consequences.

Consider a promise. It can be spoken in only a few seconds, yet its meaning reaches into the occasions on which it might be kept. Consider a letter. Its writer can finish it and send it away, but the ideas it preserves may become available again much later. Twilight's friendship reports provide an especially beautiful example when she encounters Discord's disruption. The past can contribute to the present because something of it remains accessible. And future events will be shaped by what the friends decide to do with that memory.

I would not wish to confuse this lovely account with a claim that friendship literally travels through some hidden quantum channel. It is a way of contemplating relationships, informed by mathematics and by Equestria's magic. The great arc of Twilight's story gives it a gentle conclusion. Her friends continue to meet, even when their lives have changed. Their history has not stopped growing. A friendship can be a little constellation of encounters stretching through time, with room for another light.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: harmony across four dimensions

tracks.announcement_text:
I would like to spend a little time considering six curious objects. A rainbow thread. A Wonderbolt badge. A rubber chicken. A flower. A bit. A medallion. None of these, considered apart from its history, would appear to explain the extraordinary magic they eventually help make possible.

Season four of Friendship Is Magic gives each of the six bearers an encounter in which her familiar Element becomes difficult to practice. Rarity must reckon with exploitation. Rainbow Dash must choose between a tempting opportunity and a commitment. Pinkie must remember whose joy gives a celebration its purpose. Fluttershy has to let a kindness change its form. Applejack has to acknowledge a truth that threatens a pleasing story. Twilight must decide what to do with an extraordinary power when the lives of her friends are at stake. Discord's final gift has an especially complex history because the meaning of the medallion changes with its passage from one relationship to another.

What delights me is the outward journey of these virtues. The six keys do not arise from the original friends merely gathering together and agreeing that they are good at friendship. Their qualities have to become significant in encounters with other creatures. Each object carries evidence of something learned in the wider world. When the keys are brought together, the achievement integrates those distinct histories.

There is a lovely lesson about knowledge here. A collection can be more than an inventory when its members preserve information about different events. A thread is a thread, and yet its history can give it a remarkable place in a shared story. I find the resulting transformation into the Castle of Friendship especially fitting. What was once a treasure to discover becomes a place from which further relationships can be supported. The magic creates room for another adventure, and another, and another.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: the six keys of harmony

tracks.announcement_text:
Discord is a creature with a remarkable talent for making an arrangement difficult to predict. His early encounter with the Mane Six reveals something more serious than unpredictability: the disruption of the trust through which their powers become usable together. They still possess their familiar identities and magical objects, but the way they understand and respond to one another has changed. Twilight's letters help recover access to a shared history. In that sense the recovery of harmony is a recovery of relations.

Quantum error correction provides a precise mathematical comparison. A code protects particular logical information against a specified set of errors. It is not a machine that simply replaces every input with one favored output. If we repeatedly reset different states toward the same target, the differences between them become progressively less accessible. Error correction, on the other hoof, is interesting because it can preserve the distinctions that belong to the protected information. In friendship we might ask a related ethical question. What has been disrupted, and what ought to survive our effort to repair it?

Starlight's town shows us the danger of confusing harmony with enforced equivalence. Later, Discordant Harmony shows a different side of the problem. Discord tries to remove the very eccentricities that make him recognizable, and Fluttershy does not ask him to remain that diminished version of himself. His strangeness can belong within their friendship. The value of that difference does not mean that every possible action is acceptable. Their relationship still calls for consideration.

I find this distinction wonderfully important. A friendship with a creature who never surprises you might be a very convenient arrangement. It would also leave an astonishing number of possibilities unexplored. Harmony can include disagreement, an odd question, a peculiar sense of humor, and even an inconvenient piece of information. It is the work of learning how those differences can belong to a shared world.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: discord, difference, and repair

tracks.announcement_text:
There is a transformation in Twilight Sparkle's story that I find as interesting as her becoming an alicorn. At first, she is a gifted scholar discovering the value of her friends. Later, she becomes someone who helps create conditions in which friendship can flourish among creatures whose lives are not organized around hers.

Consider a network with one central participant. Every other participant is connected to that center, but not to one another. Information can travel efficiently when the center is available. If that participant is removed, however, the network falls apart. Now imagine an arrangement with additional connections among the others. Different structures have different mathematical properties, and the appropriate design depends upon the task. In a community concerned with friendship, there is an additional reason to value those independent connections: they belong to the lives of the participants themselves. Twilight's achievement as a teacher can grow when her students become capable of acting together without awaiting her instructions.

The Young Six are a particularly lovely expression of this idea. Their response to the loss of the Tree of Harmony creates a new place for their own friendships to continue. They inherit something from the earlier generation, but they do not merely repeat its adventures. Their experiences become part of the history of harmony. And in the finale, Luster Dawn is given an opportunity to encounter the problem of friendship anew.

Meanwhile, the original friends still have their Council of Friendship. They return to each other, not because time has stood still, but because it has not. Their responsibilities and interests have developed. Their meetings give them occasions to learn about those developments and to continue creating memories together. I find that ending rather beautiful. The magic of friendship has passed from extraordinary artifacts into the ordinary rhythms of a shared life. There will be other creatures, other meetings, and other questions. There is no need for the story of harmony to conclude simply because a particular adventure has reached its last page.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: what twilight leaves to the future

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Prayer of the Corvid Circle.

Let us see the nuance where others see only a silhouette,
And understand that taxonomy is a living garden, not a static cage.

As within, so without.

My silver sigil of the fourth dimension is with you.

So mote it be, and so it is.

Amen.

tracks.announcement_text:
Come with me through the mirror, friend. Let us spend a little time with the girls of Canterlot High. Our story begins before the Fall Formal, before a crown came tumbling out of a statue, and before these girls knew how much they would come to mean to one another.

A school has a long memory. Take the two women running Canterlot High. Celestia had once walked those halls as a senior with a younger sister just starting out. She stood for school president. Luna helped with the campaign, went looking for friends of her own, and auditioned for the school play. The first Friendship Games with Crystal Prep were being organized while they were students. Years later, a girl could sit in the principal’s office worrying about an election or a friendship gone sour, completely unaware how much of it the woman behind the desk could remember from the other side.

In Equestria there was another Celestia and a very promising student. Sunset Shimmer could make a potted plant grow to an astonishing size in front of a board of examiners. Ask her to lunch afterward and she could leave five perfectly friendly ponies wishing they hadn’t bothered. She believed she was training for something important. Whatever it was, she assumed it would require extraordinary magic, and so she went back to studying the thing at which she was already extraordinary.

My lilac mane swishes with endearment, friend, at the peculiar symmetry of the two Celestias. A school can remember someone as a pupil long after it has entrusted her with the care of pupils. Sunset, meanwhile, had acquired a remarkable power without learning what to do when another pony offered her a place at the table. I wonder which of those two lessons she would have found more difficult to pass.

When Princess Celestia showed her a mirror, Sunset saw in it a version of herself she wanted desperately to become. She had wings. She looked like royalty. The lessons Celestia thought she needed and the lessons Sunset wanted now seemed to have very little to do with one another. Sunset went looking for answers in a restricted library, demanded that Celestia make her a princess, and lost her place as Celestia’s pupil. When she went through the mirror under her own power, she knew just about everything a student could dig up about it. She still had to learn what to do with a pair of hands. If she missed the ponies who’d asked her to lunch, she’d left herself a long way to go to tell them so.

Rainbow and Fluttershy already knew each other from junior high. At Canterlot’s Freshman Fair they found themselves in a photograph with Applejack, Rarity, and Pinkie Pie. Five girls fitting into a picture was easy. Getting to the point where any one of them could count on the other four took rather longer.

They landed in Mrs. Harshwhinny’s homeroom together. At lunch Rarity drew the attention of Applejack’s cousins Babs Seed and Sunflower. They admired Rarity’s clothes. They had rather less appreciation for Applejack’s, and quite definite ideas about who else should be allowed to sit down. Fluttershy got hurt in ways that would sound very small told separately. Somebody knocked her tray. Somebody sent her away from a table. Two girls she liked were standing right there when she was insulted, and neither of them said anything. Rarity and Applejack each knew how easily she could lose her own place by objecting.

Pinkie spent some time looking for a club where she could do the thing she liked best. It was at a soccer game that she finally got to do it. She won Vice Principal Luna’s permission to give the crowd a little school spirit, then went around with Fluttershy handing out Wondercolt ears and tails. Out on the field, Rainbow discovered she could do considerably more for the side when she passed the ball. Up by the bleachers, Fluttershy was interested in how Sunflower’s sick dog was getting on. Sunflower had hardly earned the inquiry. This time, when she and Babs put Fluttershy down, Rarity and Applejack spoke up. The team won. Pinkie had the beginnings of a glee club. More importantly for Fluttershy, she had two girls who’d learned something since lunch.

What interests me about that photograph is that it cannot tell us which of these girls will stand beside Fluttershy when it costs them something. A picture fixes a moment, but friendship has depth in time. I like that Rarity and Applejack had the opportunity to do something different before the afternoon was over.

In time they got an invitation to tell the school paper how they’d become friends. They gave the interviewer a very good account of themselves, including the difficult bits. Rarity shook her hand afterward. Her name was Sunset Shimmer. Long before she had any business calling herself their friend, Sunset knew exactly how those five had found one another.
tracks.title: through the mirror · 01 · before the fall formal

tracks.announcement_text:
Our next visit to Canterlot High begins on a Wednesday, with Fluttershy and a rather unexpected crown.

On Wednesdays, Fluttershy stood outside Canterlot High handing out flyers for the animal shelter. She was asking for volunteers the morning a crown came flying out of the school statue and hit her. Once she’d recovered from the surprise, she took it to the principal. It looked like the crown for the Fall Formal, and somebody was going to want it back.

Sunset Shimmer had wanted it for herself. She caught Fluttershy in the hall and demanded to know what she’d done with it. Usually, when Sunset picked on somebody, the people nearby discovered urgent business at their lockers. This time a girl with purple hair told her to leave Fluttershy alone. Afterward, Fluttershy wanted to know who the new girl was. You could tell how things had been going at school by how much that small intervention meant to her.

The girl was Twilight Sparkle. At home in Equestria she was a newly crowned princess. Here she was having a rough time opening doors. She had followed Sunset through a mirror in pursuit of her stolen crown and come out of the pedestal of the school statue with hands, two feet, and no experience using either. Her companion Spike, who had gone in a dragon, had come out a dog. Sunset understood the crossing perfectly well. She’d once been Princess Celestia’s pupil, long before she’d made a name for herself at Canterlot High. The principal now in possession of the crown looked and sounded remarkably like Celestia. That made two of them who were going to be difficult to explain to each other.

The school had already earmarked the crown for the formal. Twilight put her name on the ballot. She had until the portal closed to get home, and an electorate consisting largely of people who had seen an embarrassing video of her trying to get around on four legs.

What she did have was an ear for a story that didn’t add up. Applejack was still sore about the time Rainbow Dash had promised to bring the softball team to her bake sale. Applejack had told people they were coming. Imagine standing there beside everything you’d baked and having to answer, all afternoon, for somebody who never showed. Rainbow, meanwhile, remembered being told the date had changed. Rarity had repeatedly volunteered to help Pinkie Pie decorate, only to receive emails saying there were plenty of volunteers. Then she’d find out Pinkie had done the whole job herself. And poor Fluttershy had organized a silent auction for the animal shelter. Pinkie had arrived with fireworks and noisemakers, under the impression she’d specifically been asked to liven things up.

They’d been friends once, these five. They knew enough about one another to be particularly easy to hurt. It was perfectly believable that Pinkie might bring fireworks to a silent auction. What nobody had done was ask to see the message. Sunset had been getting between them, sometimes with little more than a change of date. Once Twilight got them talking, there were apologies to make and a dance to put back together. Rainbow even gave Twilight a chance to prove herself on the soccer field. Twilight lost spectacularly and kept playing. That suited Rainbow just fine.

At lunch the girls pulled on Wondercolt ears and tails and got the cafeteria singing for Twilight. The lovely thing about that lunch is how readily the school joined in. All those different tables, and all this time they’d had a song in common. When the decorations in the gym were wrecked and the formal might have to be postponed, the students pitched in. By then the girls had heard the business about the mirror. Pinkie took the news of a pony princess from another dimension exceptionally well.

Once the dance was back on, Rarity had just enough time to improve upon an already perfectly satisfactory evening. She finished her own makeup, looked around for another face to work on, and found Applejack’s. Applejack was pleased with the face she’d arrived in. But the others encouraged her, and she sat down. Rarity got the whole look on before Applejack took a good look in the mirror and asked if she could take a little off. Then a little more. The face Applejack finally approved of bore an extraordinary resemblance to the one she’d brought into the room. She was ready for the dance. Rarity, who’d put in a good deal of work to get her approximately nowhere, might have appreciated a moment to recover.

Twilight won. Outside the school, Sunset threatened to destroy the portal unless Twilight handed over the crown. There were people Twilight loved on the other side. Fluttershy knew this. She stood there and heard a girl she’d met only days ago tell Sunset to go ahead. Twilight had seen how much harm Sunset could do at school without magic. She was willing to lose her way home to keep these girls safe. Sunset had been bluffing, but Fluttershy couldn’t get over the fact that Twilight had meant it.

Ah, friend, I would have liked to sit beside Fluttershy when she was handing out those flyers. Consider the distance between returning a lost crown because it belongs to somebody else, and taking a crown because one believes it belongs to oneself. Neither action looks very grand in the beginning. Yet they set two lives moving toward very different futures. And when Twilight reaches into that crater, she is offering Sunset a possibility, not declaring that the harm never occurred.

In the scramble that followed, Sunset got the crown onto her own head. Its magic turned her into a winged creature who could command the students and mean it quite literally. She intended to march them through the portal. The six girls stood together against her, and the magic answered them. When it was over, Sunset was at the bottom of a crater in front of the school. A great deal of brickwork was going to need replacing.

Twilight reached down to help her up. Sunset admitted that she didn’t know how to be a friend. She sounded young when she said it. Until then she’d always made sure to sound like the person in the room who knew the most.

The music started up again inside. However much rebuilding there was going to be tomorrow, the students had done a great deal of work to put on a dance tonight.

At the dance, Photo Finish had an idea about the sort of picture these girls ought to take home. She’d already photographed Apple Bloom, Sweetie Belle, and Scootaloo, and apparently an accurate record of three girls looking nice at a school dance had failed to satisfy her. Out came the props. Twilight and Pinkie made a pair of detectives. Rainbow and Applejack found things to do in the background. Rarity got a turn in a pair of butterfly wings which, under the lights, briefly caught fire. Photo Finish came away convinced she’d done the finest work of her career. Rarity had a question before everybody packed up. Could she keep the wings? You had to admire a girl who knew exactly what she liked, even lightly singed.

Applejack had plans for the dance floor, too. Applejack got her little sister Apple Bloom up for a line dance. Rainbow and Scootaloo answered with moves of their own. The older girls got so invested in the contest that the younger ones peeled off, put together a routine, and won it. Applejack could appreciate a good dancer even when she’d just lost to one. Rainbow could appreciate a good dancer and immediately request a rematch. If you knew them, both responses had a certain warmth.

Twilight had to go home. The other five girls were still going to be there in the morning. So was Sunset. They accepted the introduction Twilight made on her way out. The next part would be theirs to work out, in a building full of people who had excellent reasons to remember what Sunset had done.
tracks.title: through the mirror · 02 · the crown

tracks.announcement_text:
Let us listen for a different sort of magic, friend, as the Rainbooms begin to find their instruments.

You could have set your watch by the way DJ Pon-3 went to school, provided your watch had a very good bass line. She put on her headphones and the crossing guard’s gestures, the baby birds opening their beaks, even a dog barking fell into time with her music. She stopped for a cupcake at the sweet shop. At school the bell rang and Principal Celestia held out a hand for the headphones. DJ gave them up without arguing. As soon as the principal turned around, out came the spare earbuds. That was the girl who would one day be able to walk through a school full of enchanted people and fetch a sound system. Her precautions that morning had been intended simply to get her as far as class.

Rainbow Dash needed a new guitar. At the music shop she got a hand on a double-necked electric at the same instant as Trixie. Applejack proposed settling it with a little playing, which gave these two an excuse to do what they’d wanted from the beginning. Trixie had the chops to make Rainbow work for it. Halfway through trying to outplay her, Rainbow found herself in the air, ears and wings out, with a charge running through the guitar she was actually playing. By the time she landed she knew which instrument she wanted. DJ could hand the double-necked one to Trixie. It was a lovely victory for Trixie right up to the moment she saw what the shop wanted for it. Twelve thousand dollars. Rainbow was already out the door.

Fluttershy made an appointment months in advance for something most people would have been happy to let somebody else do. Once a year a volunteer at the rescue center got to give the hamster habitat a proper cleaning. All those tubes needed scrubbing. Rarity came along to look after the occupants. By the time Fluttershy had finished, Rarity had named the hamsters, dressed at least one, and acquired a detailed personal account of who had chewed whose scarf. She had rather less information about how to get everybody back into the habitat.

A tambourine fell out of Fluttershy’s bag. The little heads turned. She shook it again and led her charges back in, sprouting wings and ears of her own along the way. She was beginning to find out what an instrument could do in her own hands. The audience Rarity couldn’t keep in a room would follow Fluttershy anywhere.

For some time Rainbow went around discussing what sort of person would make a good drummer, frequently in the presence of Pinkie Pie and a noise for which Pinkie Pie was responsible. During preparations for a banner, Rainbow authorized the liberal use of glitter. Pinkie tapped out a rhythm on the container and distributed it quite liberally over Rainbow. At lunch there was an entire percussion section available in the form of cutlery, trays, glasses, and people's heads. Rainbow carried on explaining how much energy a drummer needed. You began to hope, for the sake of everyone trying to finish lunch, that the answer would occur to her soon.

Rarity suggested finding somewhere for Pinkie to put all that energy. Behind a drum kit at last, Pinkie played a solo that brought out her pony ears. Rainbow was pleased with herself for having spotted the talent. Pinkie let her have that one and supplied the rimshot.

My ears perk at the thought of an instrument finding its musician. Fluttershy was not suddenly a different girl when the tambourine worked. She had spent all that time learning to be gentle with small creatures. The music gave something already present in her a way to be heard. Rarity and her grand piano, on the other hoof, might have benefited from a little advance planning.

Rarity had a related problem. She could play piano beautifully. The piano was at one end of the school, the others had booked the band room at the other, and the instrument was a grand. She enlisted the Diamond Dog boys to move it and arrived riding on top. She made an entrance the girls would remember. She also made it just in time for the end of their reservation. Practice would have to move to the gym.

Pinkie, now in a position to say something about finding the right instrument, offered her a keytar. Rarity tried it. She could play it standing up, wear it on a strap, and make sounds worth growing pony ears for. A discovery of this importance might reasonably have released the moving crew for the afternoon. Rarity accepted the keytar and asked the boys for a ride to the gym on the piano.

Applejack had a perfectly good bass already. Unfortunately, her grandmother had sold it for two dollars at a garage sale. The new owners, Flim and Flam, offered to sell it back to her for a thousand. Rarity remembered what they’d paid. The brothers seemed to feel they’d incurred some very considerable transportation expenses. The instrument even had Applejack’s initials on its strap, and still they doubted it was hers. Then they made the mistake of wondering aloud whether she could play it.

She picked up that bass and gave them their answer. Her friends helped negotiate the rest. Getting her instrument home involved a shift promoting the shop out on the sidewalk in a banana suit, where Granny Smith had occasion to discover that her granddaughter played the bass. Applejack could have wished for a more convenient moment for her grandmother to take an interest in her music.

Through the mirror, Princess Twilight missed these girls enough to imagine whole evenings with them. It was easy to picture a school party, although the difficult part was letting six different people decorate. In one such evening Pinkie’s luau came down around her, Rainbow’s sporting equipment flew about at head height, and Applejack’s rodeo bull provided excitement in excess of requirements. Rarity favored a masquerade. Fluttershy would have invited enough animals to populate a petting zoo. Twilight’s own idea looked suspiciously like additional time to study. Rainbow found room for a little of everybody’s idea, and they could finally play “Shake Your Tail!” for a party they all recognized as theirs.

Give Twilight a carnival to picture and she could find things to love about every pair that wandered off together. Applejack and Rainbow took on a test of strength and got upstaged by little Spike. Pinkie and Rarity found the cotton candy. Fluttershy approached Whack-a-Mole with a firm personal conviction that a succession of little heads popping out to see her was an invitation to pet them. There were texts back and forth, then a photo booth where everybody could fit, and finally the Ferris wheel going up into the night. Back in Equestria, Twilight could have told you exactly whom she wanted beside her at the top.
tracks.title: through the mirror · 03 · finding their instruments

tracks.announcement_text:
Now that the instruments are together, there is the considerably more complicated matter of becoming a band.

Once all five could make it to rehearsal with their instruments, you could tell whose idea the Rainbooms had been by listening to Rainbow say my band within earshot of the four other people required to make it sound good. She played lead guitar and sang. Applejack played bass, Pinkie drums, Rarity keytar, Fluttershy tambourine. Fluttershy wrote songs, too. Getting one past Rainbow and onto the set list was another matter.

Sunset hung around their rehearsals. The five had made room for her socially, a kindness she felt keenly in a school where an entire hallway might still go cold at the sight of her. She had yet to find out what she could say in that room. If Rainbow steamrolled Fluttershy, did the former school bully really get to be the one who pointed it out? Sunset often spotted trouble early and let the moment to speak pass. Everybody else had a grievance they were letting pass, too. Rarity put work into costumes that Applejack could have done without. Pinkie could remember when rehearsal had been fun.

Then three new girls arrived. Adagio Dazzle did most of the steering. Aria Blaze had a gift for getting a dig in, and Sonata Dusk could exasperate the other two at conversational walking speed. As the Dazzlings, though, they could sing together beautifully. They wore red pendants at their throats. In Equestria they had been sirens, able to feed on discord. They persuaded a cafeteria full of teenagers that the upcoming musical showcase would be much more interesting if everybody had somebody to beat.

For help, Sunset turned to a book she’d brought from home. A message written in it could appear in a companion volume in Equestria. Princess Twilight found a way to use the books to reopen the portal, and back she came, to a group of friends enormously relieved to hand the problem to her. Twilight set to work on a musical counterspell. At Pinkie’s sleepover she borrowed Fluttershy’s notebook and found one of the songs Fluttershy had written. Later, when the house was quiet, Sunset found Twilight still at it in the kitchen. It was easier for the princess to admit how stuck she felt with just Sunset there. Pinkie’s sister Maud came through for a snack for her pet rock, Boulder. Even a private conversation about saving the world had to accommodate the habits of the Pie household.

During “Awesome as I Wanna Be,” Rainbow had the room. She was enjoying herself so much that her magic began to show. Playing music with her friends could give her pony ears, wings, and a flowing tail. Normally that would have been quite a finish. With the Dazzlings watching for precisely that power, Sunset tackled her to stop the performance. To Rainbow it felt like public humiliation. To Sunset it was one more occasion on which doing something about a problem had made everybody look at her the old way.

The argument finally happened underneath the stage, where a furious Trixie had trapped the Rainbooms. Above them, the Dazzlings were having a wonderful evening. Below, Fluttershy finally said what it was like to write a song and never get to hear her friends play it. Twilight admitted how much pressure she was under. Sunset told them what she’d seen happening between them and what had kept her quiet. There was time, at last, for the girls to hear the ends of one another’s sentences.

The silver sigil on my flank glimmers with quiet affection, friend. Fluttershy's song did not become good when Rainbow finally chose it. It was good in the notebook. The difference was that the other girls had learned how to listen. And Sunset, who had once made a great art of controlling people, had something quite different to contribute when she was finally invited up to sing.

They got out with help from Spike and DJ Pon-3, whose headphones had kept the sirens out of her head and whose sound system could make up for a lot of lost ground. They still had to choose a song. Rainbow picked the one Fluttershy had written. Fluttershy made a little sound of pure delight. Then Applejack turned to Rarity. If they were going to do this, she wanted those stage outfits. By the time Twilight called Sunset up to sing with them during “Welcome to the Show,” each girl had heard something from a friend that she’d been waiting a long time to hear. A girl who’d spent rehearsal wondering whether she had permission to speak had an audience now, and she sang. Together the Rainbooms shattered the sirens’ pendants. Left to sing without magic, the Dazzlings made a rapid exit.

Princess Twilight went home again. Sunset stayed with the band, singing and playing guitar. She could write to Twilight when she needed her. She also had people close enough to hear her without the help of an enchanted book.

Sunset still remembered the photographs of herself in Principal Celestia’s office. There she was, the reigning princess at one Fall Formal after another. A girl passing them on her way to see the principal could have come away with the idea that these had been the happiest nights of Sunset’s life. Sunset could look at the very same pictures and remember how much work she’d put into making other girls afraid to run against her. She took the old pictures down.

I have a particular fondness for the image of Sunset on that roof. A memory need not be denied for the person who carries it to change. Those photographs are evidence of a real past; the song is evidence of a real present. Both belong to her life.
